slides.headline: Born on September 8th, the voice that carried Assam to the rest of India.
Bhupen Hazarika
slides.body: Born in Sadiya, Assam in 1926, Hazarika cut his first record at age 10, then went on to earn a PhD in mass communication from Columbia University before returning home to build a career as a singer, songwriter, filmmaker and public intellectual.

slides.headline: Songs that crossed languages, not just states.
slides.body: Hazarika wrote mostly in Assamese, but his songs on humanity and universal brotherhood were translated and sung across India for decades - carrying a regional voice into a truly national one, well before streaming or social media could do that work for him.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A developed India includes every region's voice, not just its capital's.
slides.body: Hazarika was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2019 - proof that the country's growth story has always needed builders working in every language and region, not just the ones that dominate the headlines.
